column1: # Requirements for Mica::YAML (milestone M4): the YAML 1.2.2 specification

column3: Input is UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32; control characters other than tab and line breaks are rejected
The encoding is detected from the byte order mark or the first bytes
Indentation is spaces only; a tab is separation, never indentation
A comment starts at a line start or after white space
%YAML and %TAG directives are read; reserved directives are ignored
Anchors and tags are attached to nodes, with tag handles resolved
An alias refers to the most recent node with its anchor; an undefined alias is an error
Double-quoted escapes, single-quoted quotes and plain scalars with line folding
Flow sequences and mappings, single-pair mappings and empty keys and values
Literal and folded scalars with indentation and chomping indicators
Block sequences and mappings, compact nesting and explicit keys
Document markers, bare documents and streams of several documents
The failsafe, JSON and core schemas resolve plain scalars
Every case of the official test suite passes in the YAML 1.2 dialect
The libyaml dialect gives libyaml's events, marks and error messages
The << merge key merges mappings; the mapping's own keys win
PullParser reads events one at a time from a String, Bytes or IO with identical results
compose returns the node graph; parse returns values; aliases share one node
max_input_bytes stops input before it is scanned
max_depth stops block and flow nesting
max_nodes stops a document with too many nodes
max_alias_expansion stops billion-laughs and quadratic alias documents (GHSA-gmv7-hhm8-cxj5) before they expand
The work budget and the deadline stop a parse with a typed, positioned error
Deep flow nesting scans in linear work
Many and long simple keys scan in linear work
Long scalars, comments and indentation runs scan in linear work
Alias fan-out composes in linear work
